raw_response:
Looking at my situation here in Quzhou County — I grow what my father grew, and his father before him. This land is good for wheat and corn. The North China Plain is made for the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. Everyone in the village does it, and for good reason. My 8 mu of contracted land will all go into wheat starting October, then flip straight to corn after June harvest. Same land, two harvests, one year.

For wheat, I'll buy improved seed from the township supply cooperative — probably the Jimai variety they've been pushing. I know the old seeds but the improved ones yield better and resist disease. I'll rotary-till before planting to work in last summer's corn stubble. I apply base fertilizer at seeding, then come back with urea in spring when the plants wake up. I irrigate four times — the winter freeze-water before the ground locks up, then three times in spring and grain-fill. I've got to spray herbicide early, then watch for powdery mildew and aphids around heading time.

For corn, I switch to hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop says is moving well this year. After I combine the wheat, I'll direct-seed the corn without tilling to save time and keep moisture. One big urea top-dress when the corn is knee-high. Usually only need one irrigation unless July turns dry. Spray herbicide and one round for corn borer.

I won't grow vegetables beyond a small patch behind the house — that's just for eating, not worth counting in the plan.
